title: The command bar: search by meaning and keyword, with the catalogue, filters, send-to-agent and new-issue offer

spec.markdown:
## Summary

The command bar. One bar in Dispatch: you press `Cmd+K` anywhere, start typing, and it unfolds what already exists - hits by keyword and by meaning in one ranked list - and what this page lets you do: the actions it offers, the operators and filters, an offer to file what you typed as a new issue when nothing matches, and an offer to hand the request to the agent that claimed the issue. The search is the heart of it, fixed and measured here. The model-driven half of the bar - the written answer, the operations it runs with undo, and the charts - is dispatch://INFRA-1588, built on this search and gated on the agent-infra model deployment.

The research behind it is dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/research-magic-bars-md, and the measured state of search today is dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/search-baseline-md.

## What this issue delivers, and what moves to INFRA-1588

This issue delivers the command bar's SEARCH HALF: the search in full - keyword and meaning in one hybrid path, since the production embedder is live (dispatch://INFRA-394) - its ranking, the index across every kind, the coverage route, the operators and chips, and broadening; and the bar and its context chip, the catalogue, the send-to-agent action, and the new-issue offer. Requirements R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R7, R10, R14, R16, and every check that serves them, including meaning recall (k24) and the production hybrid ranking (k17), which wait on no model deployment, only on production carrying the merged build.

The CHAT-MODEL ANSWER HALF moves to dispatch://INFRA-1588: the written answer and its streaming, operations with undo, the confidence thresholds, the run trace, the agentloop wiring, the decision-model bake-off, the unconfigured-capability route, the typed blocks and charts, and the status answer - requirements R6, R8, R8a, R9, R11, R12, R13, R17, R18. It is gated on the agent-infra deployment that configures Dispatch's decision and writing models (dispatch://INFRA-1281 and dispatch://INFRA-1496, the chain dispatch://INFRA-1502 drives); the search embedder it does not wait on, because that is already live. The vision below describes the whole bar for context and still names those requirements by their labels; this issue is accepted on the search-half requirements and their checks alone.

## Two tiers, two panels

Nobody who is fast puts a model in the keystroke path. Linear's bar is lexical and matched in the browser against a store the client holds. Notion runs two bars on two keys and its model tier is seconds to minutes, visibly working. Superhuman's published budget is under 50 ms. So:

**The fast tier, while you type.** Hits from the index, the actions this page offers, your recent items when the input is empty. No model call.

Half of this tier exists already: the palette paints this page's actions from memory with no network call. The half that does not is the rows that name items, the hits and the recents for the words typed, which today wait on the whole hybrid `GET /api/v1/search` at p50 1,034 ms, the embed call's cost. Its keyword-only path answers in tens of milliseconds, more than thirty times faster, so the bar type-aheads straight off it with no browser-held store: the client caches only the person's recents and the last result sets. The keyword hits paint on each keystroke with no model called; the meaning leg — the embedding and the fused re-ranking — runs once after a short pause in typing (about half a second), not on every keystroke and not only on Enter, and leaves the person's recents and last result sets cached in the client, nothing more. Enter opens the row the person is on; it never re-ranks. When a re-rank drops the highlighted row, nothing is left highlighted, so the next Enter cannot open a row the reader never chose. Making those keyword rows fast is what the bar is judged on.

**The agent, as you pause.** It arrives in its own panel beside the hits and streams as you type, after a short pause, not only on Enter: an answer with the items it used, an offer to make an issue, or an offer to send this to the agent that claimed this issue. When your words are a command, it shows what it will do and, above the confidence threshold, runs it on submit, at once and with undo, never on a pause (R8). Two panels, the hits always there and the answer building beside them, the slower half visibly working, never a second product.

:::ask{#7f5ce06f-8e20-4027-a6dd-b5da1966bf43 urgency="high" multiple="false" state="answered" answered_by="sami@theorem.dev" answered_at="2026-11-06T16:04:35.802329Z" selected="["Model decides, gated by confidence"]"}
When the best answer to a typed question is a chart - "issues closed per week", say - v58 draws one only when you ask for a chart in words (R6, R17); the model never draws one on its own. You asked whether the routing model should decide that. Should the routing model choose the chart display when a chart is the right answer, above its confidence threshold, or stay with charts only on an explicit request? Recommendation: let the model decide - the bar's job is to answer the question, a chart is sometimes the answer, and it sits in its own panel above the confidence threshold so a wrong call is not intrusive and undo bounds it; the cost is an occasional unwanted chart and the chart-spec call's latency, both gated by confidence.

- Model decides, gated by confidence: the routing model draws a chart when it is the right display above its threshold; a wrong call is a non-intrusive panel with undo, at the cost of a chart-spec call and the odd surprise chart.
- Only on an explicit request (v58): a chart appears only when you ask for one in words; no surprise and no extra call, at the cost of missing the chart when it is the best answer and you did not think to ask.
:::

:::ask{#c7745306-4da6-4d80-8af2-786d814b9f27 urgency="high" multiple="false" state="answered" answered_by="sami@theorem.dev" answered_at="2026-11-06T16:05:09.82891Z" selected="["Keep the server keyword path (v58)"]"}
The fast tier's item hits come from the server's keyword path, measured at 28 ms median and 237 ms at the 95th percentile over a workspace of production's size, with the browser holding only your recents and last results (R2). You thought the browser-side store was what made it Linear-fast. Linear holds its whole dataset in the browser and matches locally with no network - instant on any connection, but only for what the client holds. Keep the server keyword path, or add a browser-held store on top for local-first matching? Recommendation: keep the server keyword path - 28 ms is already under the 50 ms instant bar and covers the whole graph, while a browser store is instant only for the recents and results already fetched and adds a snapshot, deltas and freshness to maintain; it is additive work on top of what is built, not a change to it.

- Keep the server keyword path (v58): 28 ms median over the whole graph, no client store to sync or stale; slower than local-first on a poor connection, where the p95 of 237 ms and p99 of 1.5 s show.
- Add a browser-held store, Linear-style: local-first matching with no network for cached items, instant on any connection, at the cost of partial coverage (only what the client holds), a snapshot and delta path, and keeping it fresh.
:::

## What is in context, and you can see it

The bar carries a chip for what it will act on, seeded from where you opened it: this issue, this document, this block, these selected issues, this project, nothing. `Tab` narrows it, `Backspace` widens it. GitHub and Attio both do this and it is the difference between a bar that guesses and one you can trust before pressing Enter.

## The catalogue is generated; the matching is modelled

Dispatch already declares everything that can be done, in one place: the route table the server mounts, whose every mutating row a test holds in exact correspondence with what it registers. The catalogue the bar ships on is the twenty mutating tool specs among the thirty-three `packages/contracts` declares, each with its `DispatchToolSpec.arguments` schema that `dispatchToolSchema` builds and its plain-words description. Which of the thirty-three mutate is not a field the tool spec carries; it is the classification the server already pins against its route table (`TestEveryMutatingRouteIsClassed`), and this tree adds a test tying the tool-spec catalogue to that mutating set, so the agent can name no action the server lacks and a new route cannot be silently missing. An action reaches the list only when its required arguments can be filled from the context, the typed words or a field in the bar. A schema for the routes the specs do not yet cover, and any growth past these twenty, wait until a verb a person types asks for them.

Twenty actions is a list the agent reads whole, under the thirty-to-fifty loaded actions beyond which a model's choice measurably falls apart. A meaning-search over the catalogue — worth about ten points of accuracy back once the list is long, where a keyword shortlist is worse than none — waits until the catalogue grows past that cliff, not before.

An action reaches the list only when the bar can fill every argument it requires, from the context, the typed words, or a field you complete inside the bar. Otherwise it is not offered. That is Apple's rule for Spotlight and it is why their actions do not fail halfway.

## What runs, and what asks first

The bar acts at once when it is confident, and gives you undo, rather than listing the operations for approval first: the evidence is that a prompt per step trains people to click through, and you chose speed over a preview (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/c60a4b39-f0d7-45a0-897c-131a4187509c). A mid-typing pause re-ranks the hits and streams the answer; a write runs when you submit, never on a pause. Above the confidence threshold it runs the operation and shows what it did, each line naming the issue, the field, the value before and the value now; below it, it offers the two best actions and runs neither until you pick one. Two writes always ask, whatever the confidence: handing a request to a live agent, and filing a new issue. Undo reverts by the same route where one exists - a field, a document version, an ask, an approval - closes a created issue with the reason, and for a sent message, a project, an artifact or a handoff records the undo rather than erasing it, since no route deletes a comment or an issue; so an irreversible write leaves a trace, the accepted cost of acting first (R8).

And a setting that puts a confirm step back before each write stays available, off until you turn it on.

## The interaction is a node

Each use of the bar is recorded: what you typed, where you typed it, what it found, what it proposed, what you approved and what each write did, linked to the items it touched. dispatch://INFRA-1588 stores the run as a caller-private `going_runs` table, the pattern Dispatch's own `me` routes already use, so you can go back through your own history and a run that went wrong is readable afterwards. Making the run a first-class node of the graph — searchable like everything else, with the node kind and visibility that needs — is dispatch://INFRA-1098's graph-model work, which this tree does not pre-empt.

## Fixing search, which is most of the complaint

The bar is only as good as what it reads, and search was weak for four reasons, all of them in the code (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/94a88637-b22c-445a-aff0-c072f2074637): an issue's keyword text was its key and title alone; the words leg ANDed every word, which the meaning leg hid at the surface, since the long question beat its own three strongest words 85% to 64% in the measurement; the five kinds were ranked in five separate lists and merged by position, so relevance across kinds was erased; and nothing reranks. This tree has fixed three of the four on `legion/INFRA-1042` (pull request #2809): the issue's own row now carries its spec text, every match is scored on one length-normalised list across the kinds, and broadening is now a fallback that fires only when the query as typed returns nothing and then only to its rarest words with `-word` subtracted, not the flood past five words the measurement found. The reranker is the fourth, and the re-baseline below settled it: it is not built.

Measured on production, 837 cases over 338 issues in 15 projects (dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/search-baseline-md): a sentence out of an issue's own spec finds that issue first 2.5% of the time and not at all in the top fifty 26% of the time, while 69.8% of the time the first hit is that issue's own document. A reworded title finds its issue first 30.6% of the time. Answered asks, searched in their own words, come first 81.8% of the time: the record of past decisions is the part that works.

The work, in the order the measurement puts it:

- **An issue carries its own spec's words — done.** This was the biggest single defect of the keyword leg. The issue's own row now carries its spec text (migration `20261105145242_issues_search_spec`), so a sentence from an issue's spec finds the issue and not only its document; the meaning leg already carried it (migration `0140_issue_embedding_spec`).
- **No reranker.** A reranker reorders what retrieval already returned; it cannot pull in an issue retrieval left out of the top fifty, which is a recall failure the spec-in-keyword fix above addresses. The re-baseline settled it: of the kind-one cases whose issue is absent from the top fifty, none has any item of its issue in the page to reorder, so a reranker has nothing to work on, and Azure's 48.4 to 60.1 on another corpus does not transfer. It is not built.
- **Index today's kinds; the rest is INFRA-1098's.** The five kinds the index covers — issues, documents, comments, asks, messages, with blocks as windows — are complete, the coverage route reporting zero lacking across the five kinds. Components and sessions, which the loader resolves but nothing indexes, and the new kinds (document versions, results, handoffs) carry a per-kind cost dispatch://INFRA-1098 owns; the coverage route names them as not indexed rather than hiding them, and they are added when that lane adds them (R5).
- **Fix the ranking — done.** One list across the kinds, not five merged by position, length-normalised.
- **Make the query do what people type.** The exact query runs as typed; only a query that would return nothing broadens, and then to its own rarest words with `-word` still subtracted — a fallback, not the default, because the measurement showed broadening every long query floods half the corpus and loses the right row. The status, author and date filters are done; what remains is the bar UI that shows the operators and offers a project, a status, an author and a date as chips (R16).
- **Measure it.** A golden set built from real searches of yours and of agents, with the top results of every configuration labelled, scored before and after. dispatch://INFRA-139 and dispatch://INFRA-300 fold in here; the controller closes them into this issue.

## Where the model runs

One Go package, imported by Dispatch's backend and by the daemon, so there is one agent loop and not two. dispatch://INFRA-204, which you approved and which is now running, is the other caller; the shared package is `agentloop` (dispatch://INFRA-1311) and both build to its interface.

The fast decisions — which action, which context, is this a question or a change, and which display the answer takes, prose or a chart — are a small decision model, and they are one call, so the display choice costs no second round trip (R6, R8a). Jev fits: typed questions, calibrated probabilities, no free text to parse. Measured from a worker pod in the cluster over 60 bar-shaped requests on a twelve-action catalogue: 91.7% right, p50 110 ms, p95 188 ms, and every wrong answer below 0.72 confidence (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/0493c6a3-4768-4018-87d7-318f3ebfb96d). That is one candidate on one small set by one labeller; R12's table decides, and Gemini Flash and the rest are measured the same way from Dispatch's own pod.

Writing the answer is a different job from deciding, and goes to a writing model on the same shared package; the answer and any typed block spec are that call's structured output.

## The order this lands in

Four lanes agreed one order on 2026-11-05, written down at dispatch://INFRA-635/artifact/refactor-plan-md. This tree sits late in it on purpose; its branch has begun — the search work of the items below is committed on `legion/INFRA-1042`, pull request #2809, and the first of the three items below has merged as `b52eddae7`, pull request #2812 — so what is left of the order is still free to change.

Before this tree merges: dispatch://INFRA-635's zod-first move must land, which `going.ts` builds on (its pull request is open, not merged); and dispatch://INFRA-1196's issue-page redesign, which R1's context assumes, must be in place. Nothing here is written against dispatch://INFRA-1098's types: R5 defers its kinds and R9 its visibility to that lane.

Then two issues of this tree, and this one:

1. In Legion's own repository, dispatch://INFRA-1279, done and merged as `b52eddae7`, pull request #2812: Dispatch's server calls a configured text-generation model, and the three going routes are up: `POST /api/v1/going/requests` answers with the request's id, `GET /api/v1/going/requests/{id}/stream` carries the answer's events (the POST's idempotency layer does not itself stream), and `GET /api/v1/going/capability` beside them. It added the settings rows, the model client, the Pulumi input and its rendering, and its merge released the `envoy-infra` plugin and the Dispatch image the next issue needs, which is why it was not part of this issue's own pull request: this pull request merges last and nothing in the tree can build on it. What it did not add is a frame for a typed block: `packages/contracts/src/going.ts` on main declares `text`, `item`, `cut`, `changed`, `none`, `end` and `error`, and no block frame. That frame is future work of dispatch://INFRA-1588, required by R6, R17 and R18 before a block of any kind can reach the page, and it is one frame on a stream that exists: the chart spec rides it after the prose frames, so an answer with no block pays nothing a reader sees.
2. In theorem-labs/agent-infra, the gate on dispatch://INFRA-1588 and not a step this issue's order waits on: `dispatch-models/` declares the two chat deployments and the chat role, which a person with Azure Owner applies, and `dispatch/` names the chat model to Dispatch. What this issue needs from that repository is not this apply but the `dispatch/` pin of the released plugin and of the image built from this issue's merge, which the production record and the after-merge production runs name.
3. This issue: the command bar's search half - the search and its fixes, the bar and its context chip, the catalogue data it serves, send-to-agent, the page-filled operators (Close issue, Reopen, Set priority — offered when the page fills the argument, run by Enter) and the new-issue offer - which this issue's own pull request delivers, building on the search meaning leg that is already live. The block frame a typed block rides, the cancellation of a superseded stream, and the measurement against the chat model belong to the answer half (dispatch://INFRA-1588), which waits on the chat deployment; this issue waits on none of that and ships once its search half is proven. The catalogue's model-chosen offer — an action chosen from the catalogue by reading your words — belongs to the answer half (dispatch://INFRA-1588), because choosing needs the model loop, which is not deployed; this issue serves the catalogue data, its route-table correspondence and its caller as the committed, tested, uncalled surface that loop will consume, and INFRA-1588 adds the argument translation and the per-action execution test. That move is recorded on INFRA-1588.

The new node kinds (a document version, a recorded result, a handoff) and per-node visibility are not this tree's work: R5 and R9 defer them to dispatch://INFRA-1098, which owns the graph registry and the visibility model.

## How production takes this change

A merge to theorem-labs/agent-infra's main applies `dispatch/`, so the model's settings reach production with that merge. Dispatch's own image is pinned in that same directory, and `dispatch/roll-image.sh` moves the pin while `dispatch/image-hold` holds it, so a merge to Legion's own repository does not reach production by itself. The production record of this issue therefore names the running build, and the first look of the production check opens the pull request on theorem-labs/agent-infra that pins the image built from this merge.

## Decisions

The decisions are in dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/decisions-md.

## Requirements

:::requirement{#r1}
**R1.** One bar opens from any page with `Cmd+K` on a Mac and `Ctrl+K` elsewhere, also while the person writes in a document, and `/` and `g p` open the same bar. It carries a chip naming what it will act on, taken from where it was opened. After dispatch://INFRA-1196's redesign the issue page is one route, `/issues/KEY`, so the things that can be in context there are the issue and its whole tree, one node of that tree (a requirement, a check, a decision, an ask, a comment, a message or a document node), and the document holding the focused node. The active preset, a saved query over the tree, is in this requirement as a sequence and not as work this issue skips: no preset type is published yet, so the preset enters the chip when its owning lane publishes it, and nothing here is built against an unpublished type. The selected issues come from the issue list, which has no selection today and gains multi-select here, and the eight tabs go, so no tab is ever context. `Tab` narrows that chip, `Backspace` widens it. With an empty input the list holds the person's recent items - the items this person last opened, kept by the browser so no new route is added - and the actions this page offers. From: dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/1f3ad09d-4e31-43a9-b2d6-4ec23674e348.
:::

:::requirement{#r2}
**R2.** The rows that name items — hits for the typed words, and the person's recent items when the input is empty — answer fast — the keyword path's measured median of 31 ms on this tree's fixture of production's size, the 45 ms median the requirement holds the bar to (the server's own time for the request; a browser paint time in CI is noise and this does not measure it) — the 28 ms earlier figure was read off a fixture whose issues.search held key and title alone, before this tree put each issue's spec into that vector, and is not this tree's number. Its 95th and 99th percentiles are reported, not held to a ceiling: two of the measured cases match tens of thousands of rows and cost seconds whatever the search does, so a tail ceiling would fail at random — over a workspace of at least today's size, with no model called to produce them. The action rows already paint from memory and are not what this measures. The hits come straight from the keyword path of `GET /api/v1/search`, which this tree adds to the route as a keyword-only request: the route carries no such request today, and without it a request embeds whenever the embedder is configured, as production's is. That request is new, so the 28 ms earlier figure is the keyword path's earlier measurement on a smaller vector and not a recorded result of it; k2 holds the new request to the 45 ms median on the rebuilt fixture of production's full corpus, reports its tail rather than holding it to a ceiling, and records what it measures on the pull request, against the 1,034 ms a hybrid round costs. The bar type-aheads off that request, debounced, and the embedding and the fusion run once after a short pause in typing, not on every keystroke, and the fused ranking they produce replaces the list with a fresh order, and the highlight stays on the row it was on rather than on a position; a re-rank that drops that row leaves nothing highlighted, so Enter opens nothing until the reader arrows. Enter opens the highlighted row and never re-ranks. Whether that pause trigger holds or reverts to Enter is the decision below. There is no browser-held replica of the issues and documents, with its delta route, cursor, paging bound and per-actor cache: the client keeps the person's recent items - the items they last opened, in the browser, so no new route and no per-item write - which this tree adds, and the last result sets `SearchPalette`'s query cache already holds. From: dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/1f3ad09d-4e31-43a9-b2d6-4ec23674e348, "very fast".
:::

:::ask{#f588bcdd-db28-4ad4-a209-ad2f8b6583c3 urgency="high" multiple="false" state="open"}
The meaning re-rank - the embedding and fused re-ranking of the hits - runs on what trigger? R2 as you approved it runs it on Enter, never behind typing. In a later latency rework I changed the trigger to a pause (the meaning leg re-ranks about half a second after you stop typing), and the code and tests on pull request #2809 build that; I did not bring the change back to you, which was my miss. It cannot simply stay as you approved it, because Enter already acts on the highlighted row - it approves a send to an agent (R10) and accepts a new issue (R14) - so one key cannot both re-rank and act, and one of the options below has to give. Recommendation: (a) the pause; it is built and green on #2809, it matches the answer panel, which already arrives on a pause, and it is what fast bars in the field do - but it does change your choice from Enter to a pause, which is why it is yours to make.

- Re-rank on a pause: about half a second after you stop typing; Enter acts on the highlighted row. Built and green on #2809.
- Enter re-ranks only when no row is highlighted: once hits show, a row is highlighted and Enter acts. Cost: the trigger is rebuilt, and the meaning leg then rarely fires, because a row is almost always highlighted.
- A separate key for the re-rank: Enter still acts. Cost: a new key to learn, and the trigger rebuilt.
:::

:::requirement{#r3}
**R3.** An issue key finds its issue as the first row in each of its forms: `INFRA-1042`, `infra-1042`, `INFRA 1042`, and the bare number `1042`, which finds the issue of the project in context and, with no project in context, each project's issue of that number. From: [the first version of this document](dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/spec@v1).
:::

:::requirement{#r4}
**R4.** Search finds the item, not only its neighbour. The query as typed runs first and answers alone whenever it matches anything, whatever its length; only an answer with no rows at all runs again over the query's rarest words, taken by ascending document frequency from the `search_term_stats` the related-item check already weighs its terms by, with `searchBroadenWords` bounding how many of those words the second run takes rather than being a length threshold. Measured keyword-only, no embedder, on the committed kind-one and kind-three cases of dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/search-baseline-md — 713 of the 837, of which 712 ran, one kind-one case refused because the fixture no longer holds its document version — against a fresh fixture of production's full corpus: the defect this tree exists to fix — an issue's own document returning while the issue itself does not — falls from 69.8% at rank one to 0% at every depth; a sentence of an issue's own spec puts that issue at rank one at least 84% of the time, in the top three at least 90%, in the top twenty at least 94%, and out of the top fifty at most 5%, where its rank-one was 2.5% and its out-of-top-fifty 26.3% before this tree. An answered ask searched in its own words is in the top three at least 84% of the time and at rank one at least 80%; the earlier floor of 95% at rank one overstated it, since the hybrid baseline with meaning search live was 81.8% at rank one, so that floor was never reachable on this corpus and meaning search did not move this kind. These floors are the keyword-only fast tier's, the path a keystroke takes; the full recall is the hybrid path, which the bar runs on a pause in typing and production serves, and the production run after the merge (k17) measures it at each of these depths beside them. No reranker is built: of the kind-one cases whose issue is absent from the top fifty, none has any item of its issue in the page, so retrieval either finds the issue or returns nothing of it and a reranker would have nothing to reorder into place. A reworded title finding its issue is the meaning index's work (R5) — a spec sentence, not the title, already finds the issue more than four fifths of the time — and is not a floor this keyword harness measures: a reworded title's paraphrase text is a model-written query, not a sentence of any document, so it cannot be re-extracted from the fixture and does not ride the committed descriptors the other kinds do, and the deployment's own paraphrases name issue subjects that cannot enter this public repository. Meaning recall - meaning search's own contribution on the cases words alone miss - is measured after the merge on production, against the same run sent as the keyword-only request (k24). From: dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/d944a690-d4c6-4e8d-967b-282c0df901c4; the measured floors, the commands and what is not measured are recorded at dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/270331b7-7fec-40be-bf87-c730b376755c.
:::

:::requirement{#r5}
**R5.** Search indexes the graph's nodes, by words and by meaning, in one path rather than a leg per kind, over the five kinds the index covers today — issues, documents, comments, asks and messages, with each kind's blocks indexed as windows under it. The node loader resolves eleven kinds in all (those five plus components, sessions and the four block kinds); components and sessions are indexed nowhere, and the coverage route names every kind it does not cover rather than hiding it. An issue's spec text now lives on the issue's own row and a document's blocks on the document, so the measured cases search well. Indexing the kinds the bar does not need — components, sessions, and the kinds the loader does not resolve at all (a document version, a recorded result, a handoff) — is  the per-kind cost dispatch://INFRA-1098 owns, not a toll the bar pays three times for cases no one measured. The coverage route reports those kinds as not indexed rather than silently absent, and the lane that owns the registry adds them with their arms when it adds them. A write is searchable within 60 seconds, and a backfill covers what exists. Meaning recall - meaning search's own contribution on the subset the keyword leg leaves outside the top three, scored against the same run sent as the keyword-only request - is measured after the merge on production (k24), where the embedder is live; it waits on no model deployment, only on production carrying the merged build. From: dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/a3e9f038-81d6-4954-8b48-caef1c80ccdf.
:::

:::requirement{#r7}
**R7.** The agent's catalogue of actions is the tool specs that already exist in `packages/contracts` — the twenty that mutate among the thirty-three, each with its zod argument schema and its plain-words description, which already generate the CLI agents use to operate Dispatch all day. Which of the thirty-three mutate is not a field the tool spec carries; it is the classification the server already pins against its route table (`TestEveryMutatingRouteIsClassed`), and this tree adds a test tying the catalogue to that mutating set, so an action the catalogue does not hold is refused, never attempted, and a new route cannot be silently missing. An action reaches the list when its required argument is filled by the page — Close, Reopen and Set priority on the issue a page names — which the bar's palette already offers and a browser check proves. The form where an action is chosen from the catalogue by reading the typed words moves to dispatch://INFRA-1588 with the model loop that chooses. This issue serves the catalogue and holds it in correspondence with the route table, the zod schema and the unknown-action refusal: GoingCatalogue, GET /api/v1/going/catalogue, GoingCaller.Do, chooseGoingRoute and checkGoingArguments stay as the committed, tested surface, with no caller outside their tests, and k7 proves them. What INFRA-1588 adds is the argument translation dispatch-execute performs — so Do sends what each real route accepts — and the test that each of the twenty examples executes against the served table, built with the loop that calls them. The catalogue does not yet carry a schema for every route, a map of which verbs apply to which kind of node, or a meaning-search over itself: twenty actions is under the count where a person cannot scan the list, and each of those is added when the action count or a verb a person types asks for it, not before. From: dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/0cc4eda8-e4e2-4b2b-ba88-dafd91e82495.
:::

:::ask{#b7f9f967-37a6-41b5-a341-5f4ff0d74fc6 urgency="high" multiple="false" state="open"}
**The catalogue's model-chosen offer and caller: here, or with the model half?** You approved R7 with the catalogue in this issue. The half that offers an action whose argument the page fills ships here (Close, Reopen, Set priority). The half where the bar reads your words and offers an action chosen from the 20-action catalogue needs the loop that chooses, which is the model half — and the chat model is not deployed. The caller that performs a chosen action (GoingCaller) sends a tool's arguments unchanged where the route expects a translation, so its correctness is proven against the loop that drives it, not here. GoingCaller.Do, chooseGoingRoute and the validators are already written and tested on this pull request and nothing calls them, so moving the work leaves them as the dormant surface and INFRA-1588 adds only the argument translation and the execution test; it deletes nothing from this branch.

Proposal: that offer clause and the caller move to dispatch://INFRA-1588 (recorded there already); this issue keeps and ships the catalogue data, its route-table correspondence, the schema, and the page-filled actions. Nothing you can see in the bar today is removed.

- Move the model-chosen offer and the caller to INFRA-1588 (recommended).
- Keep the model-chosen offer here (needs the model loop the chat deployment does not have yet, plus a bar approval surface and e2e; it duplicates the page actions for the only argument a search bar can fill without a model).
:::

:::requirement{#r10}
**R10.** The bar can hand a request to the agent that has claimed the issue, as one action in the same list as the rest. It always asks before it sends, because sending spends that agent a turn (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/4310b2c0-df6f-424b-b0b6-b75e23a60fb6); once you approve it sends and says it did. From: dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/ca3f35c7-a49d-420a-823f-a87884b76a19.
:::

:::requirement{#r14}
**R14.** When no hit is a close match, the bar offers the typed words as a new issue, and it always offers rather than filing one on its own, because a wrong issue leaves a husk. What a person types is a declaration of what they want to be able to do, so those words become that issue's first verification criterion, word for word, and not prose for an agent to restate; the spec and the plan are the working-out beneath it. Dispatch adds no text of its own, gives the issue the configured label, opens it, and starts a conversation on it with the session the settings name. Where no session is named, Dispatch makes the issue and says that none was started. From: [the first version of this document](dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/spec@v1) and dispatch://INFRA-635/comment/3417122c-d088-478f-ae47-3ee8aafbc403.
:::

:::requirement{#r16}
**R16.** The query operators that already work are shown in the bar, and the filters a person expects exist there as chips rather than nowhere. A quoted phrase, `OR` and `-word` are offered as the person types and each narrows the list it is typed into. A project, a status, an author and a date are chips the person adds to the input, each narrowing the same list, and a chip reads back in the words the person chose rather than as a query string. This requirement is here because the problem section above promises it; it is not a search-ranking requirement.
:::

## Verification

The checks are the `check` blocks of dispatch://INFRA-1042/artifact/verification-md.

decisions.markdown:
# Decisions

Every choice this design has made, with its reason. Each one a person made is linked to where he made it.

## Simplified 2026-11-06, after Sami's directive to cut over-engineering

Sami asked every architect (2026-11-05) to retract pending approvals and cut over-engineering, "do the Standard Thing". A hard review and two review rounds found this design over-built, and it was cut. Where the decisions under the later headings conflict with these, these hold.

- The item rows are **not** matched in a browser-held store. The keyword path of `GET /api/v1/search` answers two orders of magnitude inside the budget, so the bar type-aheads straight off it; the client caches only recents and the last result sets (R2).
- Search indexes the **five kinds the index covers today**; components, sessions and the new kinds (document versions, results, handoffs) are dispatch://INFRA-1098's, not the bar's (R5).
- Per-node visibility is **not this tree's**: bar runs are caller-private behind a `me` route (`going_runs`), and a general node-visibility model is dispatch://INFRA-1098's own feature (R9).
- The answer's charts render with the **ECharts already in the app**, not a second Vega-Lite stack, and are not persisted (R17).
- The project-status answer reads **stored data**; there is no live-agent fan-out, and R10 covers the live case (R18).
- The catalogue is the **~19 existing tool specs**; no per-route schema authoring, per-kind verb map, or meaning-search yet (R7).
- Undo acts with the write and reverts by the same route where one exists; a created issue is closed with the reason and a comment is recorded undone, since no route deletes either, and there is no preview (R8, superseding the earlier field-revert-only rule per ask c60a4b39).
- The model bake-off is **~80 cases, one labeller, two or three candidates** (R12).
- Query broadening is a **fallback** — only a query that would return nothing broadens, to its rarest words — not the default (R4).

### The floors, measured on the fixed tree (2026-11-06)

The root implementer re-baselined on a fresh fixture of production's content, keyword-only, and these follow from the numbers.

- The **reranker is not built**: of the kind-one cases whose issue is absent from the top fifty, 0 have any item of their issue in the page, so a reranker has nothing to reorder; retrieval finds the issue or returns nothing of it (R4). This is the re-baseline Sami's "cut over-engineering" asked for.
- **R4's floors are the fixed tree's measured numbers:** a spec sentence puts its issue at rank one at least 84% (was 2.5%), top-three at least 90%, top-twenty at least 94%, out-of-top-fifty at most 5%, and the issue's-own-document-without-the-issue defect is 0% at every depth (was 69.8%); an answered ask in its own words is top-three at least 84%, rank-one at least 80%. k4 is a regression guard: the first run passes by construction, a later run that regresses fails (R4).
- **The 95%-at-rank-one floor was never real.** The hybrid baseline with meaning search live was 81.8% at rank one, so meaning search did not move this kind and the earlier floor is revised to the measured reality, not chased with a boost (R4).
- **Kind two (reworded title) is out of the committed floors.** Its paraphrases have no committed descriptor to re-extract and each names an issue's subject, so they cannot enter this public repository, and a keyword-only harness cannot measure paraphrase recall at all; the meaning-recall capability stays in R5 and kind one already proves it (R4).
- **R2's latency is the measured median of 31 ms, held to a 45 ms median with the tail reported**: the median is keystroke-fast and the tail far inside the 1,034 ms a hybrid round costs (R2).

### Resolved in the fresh pre-approval review (2026-11-06)

- **The name is "the command bar."** Sami answered the naming ask (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/97f0bca7-afc9-45ec-b6df-ab7cae6c7cb1) with "It's the command bar." That is the display name. The lowercase code identifiers `going` — the package `packages/envoy/going`, the `going_runs` table, the `/api/v1/going/` and `/api/v1/me/going-runs` routes — stay as a built internal codename, not a product name, so no migration is forced; if the public route and table should also shed the word, that is a cheap rename a person can call for.
- **Each use of the bar is recorded as a caller-private `going_runs` table now, and becomes a first-class `interaction` graph node through dispatch://INFRA-1098's graph-model work.** This tree stores the run as the table Dispatch's own `me` routes already use, and the node kind and its visibility — which INFRA-1098 owns — make it a node. The own-runs read is a filter on the `me` route, not the graph search index, so it adds no sixth indexed kind (R9).
- **Meaning recall is measured as meaning search's own contribution, not against a paraphrase set**, by running the committed cases twice on one fixture - keyword-only and embedder-live - and scoring the subset the keyword leg leaves outside the top three, which meaning search must move into the top three at a share stated in the pull request (k24), because this deployment holds no LEGION project, so the committed LEGION paraphrases match nothing here, and new paraphrases against this corpus would name an INFRA or BET subject in a public repository. Meaning search is already live in production, so this guards that the keyword work does not regress it (R5).

### Sami's design choices (2026-11-06, ask c60a4b39)

Asked which of four choices to change from the recommendation, Sami chose all four alternatives (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/c60a4b39-f0d7-45a0-897c-131a4187509c):

- **The answer sits in its own panel beside the hits, not in one list** (the Two tiers section, R6).
- **The answer streams live as you type, after a short pause, not only on Enter** (R2, R6). The item rows stay instant on each keystroke; the model answer costs a call per pause, which he accepted. Delivering it needs the going stream to cancel a superseded run and to carry a block frame beside its text and item frames; those move to dispatch://INFRA-1588 with the answer half.
- **The answer is prose and links by default; a chart may be drawn unasked when the decision model chooses that display at or above the chart-display threshold, and every other typed block is drawn only when asked for** (R6, R17, R18). Ask c60a4b39 set the default of prose and links, and dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/7f5ce06f-8e20-4027-a6dd-b5da1966bf43 freed the chart kind from it: the display is one more typed decision of the decision model's existing call, gated by a threshold of its own fitted on that model's per-case display confidences over the labelled cases (R8a), and the prose answer is on screen beside any chart, so an unwanted one is ignorable. An explicit request for a chart is a parse of the typed words and never a confidence, and no chart is drawn, asked for or not, where no existing read fills it or the read behind it returns fewer than two points. A metric, a timeline, a table, an issue list, a progress block and an agent-status block stay on ask.
- **The bar acts at once when it is confident and gives undo, not a preview first** (R8); below the confidence threshold it offers the two best actions (R8a), and a per-person confirm setting is off by default. Undo reverts a field by the same route; a created issue is closed with the reason and a posted comment records that it was undone, since no route deletes either, so an irreversible write leaves a trace. That trace is the accepted cost of acting first, which I decided and told him he can change at approval (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/d8529ad1-6816-44e9-91ee-de9701d228ef).

## A chart is drawn unasked when the decision model chooses that display

The default answer is prose and links. The chart kind alone is free of that default: the decision model answers the display as one of the typed questions of the call that already chooses the action and the context, and a chart is drawn where that display confidence is at or above the chart-display threshold (dispatch://INFRA-1042/spec#b-r6, dispatch://INFRA-1042/spec#b-r17). The threshold is fitted on the chosen model's own per-case display confidences from R12's bake-off, by the rule in dispatch://INFRA-1042/spec#b-r8a, and the case set carries at least 20 chart-worthy cases so the fit rests on more than a handful (dispatch://INFRA-1042/spec#b-r12). The option weighed against it is a chart only on an explicit request: no surprise chart and no fit to maintain, at the cost of missing the chart whenever the person did not think to ask for one. The gate bounds the cost of the chosen option. The display rides a call that already fires on a typing pause and the chart spec rides the answer call, so an unasked chart adds no call of its own; the chart sits in its own panel beside the prose, so a wrong display is ignorable and no write follows it; and no chart is drawn where no existing read fills it or the read returns fewer than two points. Chosen at dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/7f5ce06f-8e20-4027-a6dd-b5da1966bf43.

## The item rows stay on the server's keyword path, with no browser-held store

The rows that name items come from the keyword path of `GET /api/v1/search`, measured at a median of 31 ms and held to a 45 ms median over a workspace of production's size, and the browser caches only the person's recent items and the last result sets (dispatch://INFRA-1042/spec#b-r2). The option weighed against it is a browser-held store matched locally, the shape Linear uses: instant on any connection, but covering only what the client already holds and adding a snapshot, a delta route, a paging bound and a freshness problem to keep. The measured median is already inside the 50 ms a person reads as instant, and it covers the whole graph rather than a cached part of it, so the store is additive work that buys the tail alone. Chosen at dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/c7745306-4da6-4d80-8af2-786d814b9f27.

## The design of 2026-11-04 was withdrawn and rebuilt with him

Versions 2 to 9 held a whole design, every choice made without the person who owns the work. He refused it (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/eea2e167-d5d3-4311-bf3d-7a71d77de246) and asked for the design to be worked out with him. Versions 10 onward are that conversation. The sections below separate what he decided from what this design decided.

## What he decided

**The bar reads Dispatch, not ctx-memory.** The first version's eleventh item had the bar reaching Slack, mail, GitHub and Drive through ctx-memory. No source of this issue states it: the two transcripts hold 34 recorded ideas (dispatch://INFRA-1041/artifact/idea-catalog-md) and none names it. He asked what Dispatch had to do with ctx, which has the same answer. Out, with the configurable extra source that existed only to carry it.

**Dispatch gets its own agent, and the words are "agentic".** A model loop with tools is an agent; what the work does not need is an Oh My Pi session or a Legion worker (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/0cc4eda8-e4e2-4b2b-ba88-dafd91e82495). The operations are writes to Dispatch's own database and need no live agent (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/ca3f35c7-a49d-420a-823f-a87884b76a19).

**Sending a request to the agent that claimed the issue is one offered action**, in the same list as the rest, not a second tier of the architecture. Same comment.

**The agent gets a tool that searches the schema of types and actions**, so it never invents one (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/0cc4eda8-e4e2-4b2b-ba88-dafd91e82495).

**Each use of the bar is a node in the graph**, so a person can revisit their own history: "these are all nodes in the graph. Everything is a graph" (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/ca3f35c7-a49d-420a-823f-a87884b76a19).

**Get ahead of indexing** (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/a3e9f038-81d6-4954-8b48-caef1c80ccdf), and fix search, which he called garbage and which the measurement confirmed (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/d944a690-d4c6-4e8d-967b-282c0df901c4).

**Scope is not cut**: asked how much to build first, he answered that the question was premature and that his answer would be to build them all in parallel (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/d4fd6b70-9269-4730-b476-191998141455).

**The leaked TypeSafe key is not rotated**: "Not now — It's fine" (dispatch://INFRA-1042/ask/40120134-1282-4fc3-9ce7-781e45042f9c).

## What this design decided alone

**The item rows are matched in the browser, not in the server.** Asked which, he read the question as scope-cutting and refused to answer a how dressed as a choice. Decided: the browser holds a store and matches against it, which is how Linear reaches a tenth of a second; a server round trip does not. Search alone is p50 1,034 ms today. **Superseded 2026-11-06:** there is no browser store; the keyword-only path of `GET /api/v1/search` answers inside the budget and the bar type-aheads off it (R2).

**The model searches again rather than trusting one query.** The answer can only link an item the model was given, so a floor built on the first 20 hits of one search is really a floor on that search's recall. The model gets a search tool, at most three calls. This is the agentic search the first version asks for.

**The browser runs the approved operations; the server reads each outcome.** Every Dispatch handler takes its caller from the request, so a server-side run would need a way to act for a person that does not exist. The server reads the issue rather than trusting the browser's report, because a record built on the browser's word could claim a write that never happened.

**One `PATCH` per issue, and a comment after its field changes.** The broker moves an issue's sequence number on every event, so one request per field would refuse its own second field and the bar would say the issue changed when nobody changed it.

**A status on a Legion-owned issue runs, with its consequence shown.** The daemon re-asserts only a session's status write and reads a person's as the move it is. Refusing it would be a restriction nobody ordered.

**Undo is defined per write.** No route deletes an issue or a comment, and this work adds none. **Superseded 2026-11-06 (ask c60a4b39):** the bar acts at once on submit and undo reverts by the same route where one exists, closes a created issue with the reason, and records a comment undone; there is no preview (R8).

**The bar acts only above a fitted confidence.** Measured: 60 bar-shaped requests to Jev from a pod, 91.7% right, p50 110 ms, p95 188 ms, every wrong answer below 0.72, and 35 of 60 above 0.8 with none wrong (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/0493c6a3-4768-4018-87d7-318f3ebfb96d). Below the threshold the bar offers two actions and asks.

**The measurement's corpus is read at run time, and the repository holds no Dispatch text.** This repository is public. The example set is questions and the keys that answer them; the program loads a real project's issues into a Dispatch of the commit under test.

**No cost cap, rate limit or quota.** The stream's standing rules forbid a cap nobody ordered. Cost is bounded where it costs little: the answer streams only after a typing pause, debounced, a superseded stream is cancelled, and a submitted request is at most four model calls and three searches. Updated 2026-11-06 (ask c60a4b39): the earlier 'no model call while the person types' no longer holds, since the answer streams as you type after a pause; the bound is the debounce and that per-request ceiling.

## What four lanes agreed, 2026-11-05

Sami asked the architects of this issue, dispatch://INFRA-635, dispatch://INFRA-1196 and dispatch://INFRA-1098 for one plan rather than four (dispatch://INFRA-635/comment/2e936603-48c1-4b23-9089-0cb239c054ff). INFRA-1196's architect holds the pen. What was settled, and what it changed here:

**The client store holds matchable text and a display tree's key, never stored markdown.** INFRA-635's R6 makes Go the one reader of stored markdown; a browser store of markdown would have brought that parser back. Their correction, taken. **Superseded 2026-11-06:** there is no client store of matchable text; the client caches only recents and the last result sets (R2).

**The catalogue's request schemas live beside the tool specs in `packages/contracts`**, one definition per mutating route, in the zod-first form INFRA-635's R2 establishes. Their command table is keyed by command names and does not grow to cover routes: taking the catalogue from it would have given the bar about a fifth of what a person can do. **Superseded 2026-11-06:** the nineteen mutating tool specs are the catalogue, and no new per-route schema is authored here (R7).

**INFRA-635's two moves land first**, so this tree writes once in the new layout. Nothing of this tree is built, so it reorders for free.

**The context chip derives from INFRA-1196's surfaces**: the issue and its tree, one node of it, the active preset, the document holding the focused node, and the selected issues from the issue list. The eight tabs go, so no tab is ever context.

**Document versions, results and handoffs are not graph nodes**, and this tree makes them kinds, each with its backlink arm in the same change. **Superseded 2026-11-06:** those kinds are dispatch://INFRA-1098's, not this tree's, and the coverage route names them as not indexed (R5).

**The catalogue reads both edge families.** Relation names are one global list and the typed-block attribute edges are a second family that shares no name with it; one alone is wrong about half the graph.

**Node visibility has two values, project-wide and author-only**, confirmed by INFRA-1098's owner, and lands as its own slice after the eight now in review. It is a change to the node schema and to every read path, not a search feature.

## Still open

The combined plan, with INFRA-1196's architect. This spec returns to the design gate when it lands.

**Composed Jev calls versus a single generative call, an open measurement.** Sami asked whether composing or ensembling Jev calls matches a single generative model call for the answer and the chart spec, in comparable wall time (dispatch://INFRA-1042/comment/f47f268a-863a-4df2-bbd9-16ee27f1a0a0, 2026-11-06). Method: the same bar-shaped requests, the R12 case set and a set of chart requests, run through two paths, (a) the generative model via agentloop Run, and (b) composed Jev Decide calls with the chart props fanned out in parallel, a consistency pass, and optionally several options rather than the top one, each scored for answer and chart quality and timed end to end from the Dispatch region. Run it when the bar answer path exists, where the two paths compare on the same inputs through agentloop Run and Decide with no rebuild. Not a blocker for the bar, which ships on the generative model.

**R10 adds the one catalogue action this tree authors.** R10 makes handing a request to the agent that claimed the issue one action in the same list as the rest (the spec says one action in the same list as the rest, and that it makes the catalogue uniform), and the agent-message route POST /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/messages is one of the forty-six with no tool spec. So R10 adds one deliberate tool spec for that route, and the catalogue the bar ships is the nineteen existing tool specs plus the one R10 adds, twenty in all. The decision that no new per-route schema is authored forbids auto-generating the route table, not this single approved addition R10 requires; the correspondence test names forty-five routes without a spec once R10 lands, not forty-six.
